testedState.worktreeBinding: The diagnosis inputs are uncommitted and are bound individually by SHA-256 below.

provenFacts.fact: The product orchestrator does not inject the test supervisor seam. The default Windows AppContainer supervisor therefore ran and resolved before host artifact classification.

A normally returned supervisor result proves that the child reached a terminal exit, the native result was readable and parsed, and owned AppContainer cleanup settled. The later artifact-missing classification additionally proves a safe nonnegative child exit code, but the public failure discards its value.

The post-supervisor commit fence and whole-tree assertion passed. Both the failure-only child receipt and the verification report returned ENOENT at read time; later canonical report states were not exposed because the host reports the first failure in canonical order.

An ordinary failure after the runner inner catch is armed is insufficient by itself: the catch performs a second tree assertion and returns a typed receipt, which the outer scope publishes before setting exit code 1.

The verification report is published only near the end of verifyProject with the other canonical reports. A failure or termination before or during this concurrent publication can leave verification-report absent.

excludedPaths: A detected AppContainer launch failure, wait failure, executor timeout, lease loss, native-result parse failure, cleanup failure or profile-query failure: each rejects the supervisor and would remain appcontainer-execution rather than reach artifact-missing.
An invalid or negative supervisor result code: host classification would emit artifact-protocol before the missing-artifact branch.
Successful runner completion: it requires a passed verification report.
A postcondition failure after compileWorkspace returns: verifyProject has already published the verification report.
A canonical VERIFY-ACCEPTANCE-003 failure: verifyProject publishes the report set before throwing it.
A source-controlled deletion after successful report or final-receipt publication: no such deletion exists in the traced runner, pipeline or normal AppContainer cleanup path.
A malformed or unreadable child receipt or verification report: the host would classify artifact-parse or artifact-read rather than artifact-missing.
A valid child receipt combined with the observed first missing report: the host would expose child-failed-before-artifacts or include the allowlisted child stage.

ambiguitySet.description: Bootstrap, import resolution, static module evaluation or runtime termination before the runner outer try begins. The generated executor bootstrap dynamically imports the bundled runner without a pre-import checkpoint.
process.cwd, environment/path validation or the first staging-tree assertion fails before the inner catch is armed.
A preflight or pipeline failure occurs before report publication, then the catch-time staging-tree assertion fails or the process terminates before returning the receipt.

The receipt pending-file open, write, file sync, close or rename fails, or the process terminates in that interval. A failure only after successful rename is inconsistent with final receipt absence unless an external actor removes it.

A runtime crash, OOM or external termination occurs before canonical report or final receipt publication. The executor can still return the native terminal code when the executor itself did not initiate a timeout failure.

A shared write-permission or filesystem failure prevents both publications, or an external actor removes a previously published artifact before the host read. Existing evidence records only read-time state, not publication history.

rootCauseAvailability: The exact evidence identifies an information-loss boundary: a pre-report failure or abnormal termination plus no final receipt visible at host read time. Current source and evidence cannot distinguish the ambiguity set without adding transient child progress and preserving a coarse termination class.

smallestDeterministicSuccessorProtocol.publication: Each finite checkpoint is create-exclusive, file-synced and directory-synced so the host can validate a continuous prefix without an overwrite window. bootstrap-entered must be published by a tiny mutation-specific bootstrap before dynamic import of the heavyweight runner core.
securityBoundary: No path, message, stdout, stderr, raw output, timestamp, transaction id or extensible payload.
The host maps only fixed reserved exit codes and exact finite checkpoint names.
Transient state remains under .isolated-process/child and does not enter generic WorkspacePaths, canonical Verification artifacts, success rawDigests or selector trust roots.
A checkpoint or termination class can only refine a failure. PASS still requires exit zero, no failure receipt and a complete canonical passed artifact set.
No retry is implied or authorized.

staticReview.failureAlgebraConclusion: rootCause=null; successor requires both a termination anchor and pre-import progress

decision.next: Freeze a separate implementation successor for coarse exit classification and crash-safe monotonic checkpoints. Only its own focused gate may run after static review.

invalidationRules: The diagnosis is bound to the exact manifest, failed vertical evidence, source hashes, head, tree and base recorded above.
A later progress or termination protocol may identify the runtime interval but cannot convert vertical-v3 to PASS.
Any source change requires a separately frozen implementation manifest and new evidence; vertical-v3 must not be rerun under its terminal manifest.
